rv.q: The music is immediate and brilliant, with Knight and Ndlovu reaching a soaring harmony on the swaggering Rock Me.
The songs come thick and fast and are all a delight.
Being as constricted as it is to one setting, and one point in time, inevitably sometimes Marie & Rosetta runs out of steam.
Every time they open their mouths to sing, any quibbles with the production are forgotten and the audience is rapt: finger-tapping, off-beat clapping, irrepressibly grinning.
With stirring vocals, sharp dialogue, and a moving exploration of faith, fame, and friendship, the production is both intimate and electrifying.
The combination is dynamite, and makes for an evening fit to honour the memory of two trailblazing women.
What makes the show worth seeing are these two amazing women; Beverley Knight is already a star
Above all, it celebrates Tharpe’s talent and serves justice to her name.
The songs, and Monique Touko’s direction of them, help restore momentum, elevating a sometimes static script into something resonant and musically vibrant.
A powerhouse performance from Beverley Knight makes Marie & Rosetta sing, even when the script holds it back.
It’s the two sensational performances that make the evening.
The luminous performances by Beverley Knight and Ntombizodwa Ndlovu alone are well worth the price of admission
Ultimately, Marie and Rosetta is a production elevated by extraordinary musical talent but held back by a script that never quite matches its subject’s legacy.
The two performances are electric, and it is simply a joy to see two artistes at the top of their game in a fitting tribute to forgotten pioneers.

cn.t: Critics praise this electrifying celebration of rock 'n' roll pioneer Sister Rosetta Tharpe, with Beverley Knight delivering a powerhouse, incandescent performance that elevates George Brant's heartfelt two-hander about a forgotten musical legend.
